summary: Privacy-first, self-hostable note-taking and knowledge app with block-level links, Markdown editing and built-in AI writing.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: SiYuan is a privacy-first personal knowledge management app. You write in a block-based Markdown editor, link and reference any block, and organise notes into a knowledge base, with AI writing and Q&A through the OpenAI API.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many note apps lock your data in the cloud or only link whole pages. SiYuan keeps data on your devices or your own server and lets you reference and embed individual blocks.
whoFor: People building a personal knowledge base
Self-hosters who want a private notes server
Teams of humans and agents sharing a workspace
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for fine-grained block references, a rich editor and self-hosting, with apps on desktop, Android, iOS and HarmonyOS.
requirements: Desktop or mobile app, or Docker for self-hosting
An OpenAI-compatible API key for AI features

overview: Features include block-level references and two-way links, SQL query embeds, a block-style Markdown WYSIWYG editor, formulas and diagrams, web clipping, PDF annotation links, database table views, flashcards with spaced repetition, Tesseract OCR and AI writing and Q&A via the OpenAI API.

Install from your app store (recommended for easy upgrades), from the GitHub releases page, a package manager, or run the server with Docker, Kubernetes, Unraid or TrueNAS. Since v3.7.0 the Docker image needs the serve subcommand, and you must set an access auth code.
Most features are free, even for commercial use; some require a paid membership. The code is AGPL-3.0 licensed.

steps.title: Install from your app market
steps.body: Recommended so you can upgrade in one click. Installers are also on the GitHub releases page and b3log.org.

steps.title: Run the container
steps.code:
docker run -d \
  -v workspace_dir_host:workspace_dir_container \
  -p 6806:6806 \
  -e PUID=1001 -e PGID=1002 \
  b3log/siyuan \
  serve \
  --workspace=workspace_dir_container \
  --accessAuthCode="${AuthCode:?Set AuthCode}"

steps.title: Open it
steps.body: Go to http://localhost:6806 and enter your access code.
